text:
alex: Quick question — noticed a weird oscillation on recent model canaries when tiny percent steps get rounded by our bucket allocator. We scheduled 3% -> 6% but several cohorts stayed at 0 until the next step and then jumped. Anyone else seen this? :thinking:

maria: yup, saw that during the privacy-filter rollout. It's the cohort hashing + integer percent buckets. Small fractions disappear.

sam: yep. two obvious fixes: 1) internal micro-buckets (e.g. 1/10000) so we never floor to zero, or 2) change allocation to stochastic assignment per-request (probabilistic) instead of deterministic hashing. micro-buckets keeps determinism for debugging.

alex: micro-buckets sounds promising. also thinking we should add deterministic per-cohort jitter on step transitions so cohorts don't all reassign exactly at the same tick — that sync causes spikes. e.g., jitter_ms in [-2000,2000] applied to hold timers.

maria: agreed. and add rollout guards: automatic rollback if error rate increases by >15% sustained over 10m, or if latency p50 regresses >200ms. we should expose those as defaults but allow override.

sam: UI question — do we show "microstep mode" toggle in console or keep it under advanced JSON? I lean hide by default and surface it when a user picks <5% initial step. keep console clean.

alex: telemetry needs to catch this: emit 'canary.assignment_fraction_by_cohort' and 'cohort.reassign_events'. alert if reassignments >3 in 10m or if assignment fraction variance >10%.

maria: quick config sketch (for rollout-service) — we can store percentages as thousandths internally and include jitter/hard guards. paste: 

```json
{
  "model": "my-model:v2",
  "strategy": "canary",
  "steps": [
    {"pct_thousandths": 100, "hold_seconds": 900},   // 0.1%
    {"pct_thousandths": 500, "hold_seconds": 900},   // 0.5%
    {"pct_thousandths": 1000, "hold_seconds": 900},  // 1%
    {"pct_thousandths": 5000, "hold_seconds": 1800}, // 5%
    {"pct_thousandths": 25000, "hold_seconds": 3600},// 25%
    {"pct_thousandths": 100000, "hold_seconds": 0}    // 100%
  ],
  "transition_jitter_ms": 2000,
  "guards": {
    "max_error_increase_pct": 15,
    "error_window_seconds": 600,
    "max_latency_p50_ms_increase": 200
  },
  "allocator": "deterministic-microbucket",
  "microbucket_resolution": 100000
}
```

sam: nice. microbucket_resolution 100k should avoid rounding even for tiny slices. watch memory for huge cohort maps but we can compress ranges. I'll prototype allocator + jitter and run it in staging.

alex: UX followup — console should show "expected vs actual assignment" heatmap per cohort and a small note when micro-buckets are used. otherwise folks are confused when their 0.1% doesn't show in logs. :eyes:

deploy-bot: canary started for my-model:v2 at 2359001300 :rocket:

maria: also add normalization when users submit weights that round to 99/101, normalize to 100 instead of erroring. small UX win.

sam: i'll open a PR with allocator + unit tests and add telemetry emits. tagging @maria for guard defaults.

alex: thanks — excited to see if this squashes the oscillation.
